title: Goroutines
content: A goroutine is a lightweight thread managed by the Go runtime: `go fn()`. Goroutines start almost instantly and have a small initial stack (~2KB, grows as needed). Thousands can run concurrently. To wait for goroutines to finish, use a `sync.WaitGroup`: `wg.Add(1); go func(){ defer wg.Done(); doWork() }(); wg.Wait()`. Never use goroutines without a way to know when they complete.

title: Channels — Communicating Between Goroutines
content: Create: `ch := make(chan int)` (unbuffered) or `make(chan int, 10)` (buffered). Send: `ch <- 42`. Receive: `val := <-ch`. Unbuffered blocks until both sides are ready. Buffered blocks when full/empty. Close: `close(ch)`. Range over channel: `for v := range ch {}`. Multiple channels: `select { case v := <-a: ... case b <- x: ... }`. Channels are the Go way to avoid shared-state data races.

title: Interfaces — Implicit Implementation
content: Go interfaces are satisfied implicitly — no `implements` keyword. `type Stringer interface { String() string }`. Any type with a `String() string` method satisfies `Stringer`. `fmt.Println` uses `Stringer` automatically. Empty interface `interface{}` (or `any` in Go 1.18+) accepts any value. Use type assertion: `s, ok := val.(string)`. Type switch: `switch v := val.(type) { case string: ... }`.

title: Error Handling in Go
content: Go returns errors as values: `val, err := fn(); if err != nil { return err }`. Create errors: `errors.New("msg")` or `fmt.Errorf("context: %w", err)`. Wrap for chain: `%w` allows `errors.Is(err, target)` and `errors.As(err, &target)`. Sentinel errors: `var ErrNotFound = errors.New("not found")`. Custom error type: implement `Error() string`. Avoid panic for expected errors.

title: defer, panic & recover
content: `defer fn()` schedules `fn` to run when the surrounding function returns (LIFO order). Use for cleanup: `defer file.Close()`, `defer mu.Unlock()`. `panic` stops normal execution and unwinds the stack. `recover()` inside a deferred function catches a panic: `defer func(){ if r := recover(); r != nil { log.Println(r) } }()`. Use panic only for truly unexpected, unrecoverable errors.

title: Slices — Go's Dynamic Array
content: Slice = pointer + length + capacity. Create: `s := []int{1,2,3}` or `make([]int, len, cap)`. Append: `s = append(s, 4)`. Slicing: `s[1:3]` (shares backing array!). Copy to avoid aliasing: `dst := make([]int, len(src)); copy(dst, src)`. `len(s)` = current size; `cap(s)` = backing array capacity. Grow efficiently: `s = append(s, batch...)`. Nil slice has len=cap=0 and is usable.

title: Maps in Go
content: Create: `m := map[string]int{}` or `make(map[string]int)`. Set: `m["key"] = 5`. Get: `v := m["key"]` (zero value if missing). Safe get: `v, ok := m["key"]; if ok { ... }`. Delete: `delete(m, "key")`. Iterate: `for k, v := range m {}`. Maps are not ordered — sort keys for deterministic output. Nil map panics on write — always initialize. Maps are not safe for concurrent use — use `sync.Map` or a mutex.

title: Structs, Methods & Embedding
content: Define: `type Point struct { X, Y float64 }`. Value receiver: `func (p Point) Dist() float64 { ... }`. Pointer receiver (to modify): `func (p *Point) Scale(f float64) { p.X *= f }`. Embedding for composition: `type Circle struct { Point; Radius float64 }`. Access: `c.X` (promoted from Point). Embedding is not inheritance — no polymorphism unless an interface is satisfied.

title: Generics (Go 1.18+)
content: Generic function: `func Map[T, U any](s []T, f func(T) U) []U`. Type constraint: `func Sum[T int | float64](s []T) T`. `comparable` constraint: types that support `==`. Custom constraint interface: `type Number interface { int | int64 | float64 }`. Type inference: compiler often infers type params. Use generics to avoid repeated code across types, but prefer simple interfaces when they suffice.

title: context Package
content: `context.Context` carries deadlines, cancellation signals, and request-scoped values. Create: `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background()); defer cancel()`. With timeout: `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)`. Check cancellation: `select { case <-ctx.Done(): return ctx.Err() }`. Pass context as first argument to all functions that do I/O. Never store context in a struct.

title: Packages, Modules & Visibility
content: Module: `go mod init github.com/user/repo`. Package name = directory name. Export: capitalize first letter (`Exported` vs `unexported`). Import: `import ( "fmt"; "github.com/pkg/errors" )`. Blank import side effect: `import _ "net/http/pprof"`. `init()` runs before `main()`, once per package. Multiple `init()` functions allowed. Avoid circular imports — restructure into shared packages.

title: Testing in Go
content: File: `foo_test.go`, function: `func TestAdd(t *testing.T) { ... }`. Fail: `t.Errorf("got %d, want %d", got, want)`. Table tests: `tests := []struct{in,want int}{{1,1},{2,4}}; for _, tt := range tests { t.Run(..., func(t *testing.T){ ... }) }`. Run: `go test ./...`. Coverage: `go test -cover`. Benchmark: `func BenchmarkAdd(b *testing.B){ for i:=0;i<b.N;i++{ Add(2,3) } }`. Subtests with `t.Run` are parallelizable.

title: Synchronization with sync Package
content: `sync.Mutex`: `mu.Lock(); defer mu.Unlock()`. `sync.RWMutex`: multiple readers or one writer. `sync.Once`: execute a function exactly once: `once.Do(func(){ ... })`. `sync.WaitGroup`: `wg.Add(n); go work(); wg.Wait()`. `sync/atomic` for lock-free operations: `atomic.AddInt64(&counter, 1)`. Detect races: run tests with `-race` flag.

title: HTTP Server with net/http
content: Handler: `func handler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { fmt.Fprintln(w, "Hello") }`. Register: `http.HandleFunc("/", handler)`. Serve: `http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil)`. Custom mux: `mux := http.NewServeMux()`. JSON response: `json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(data)`. Read body: `json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&payload)`. Set header: `w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")`.

title: Composition over Inheritance
content: Go has no class hierarchy — use composition. Embed structs: `type Logger struct { prefix string }; type Server struct { Logger; port int }`. The server gets all Logger methods promoted. Use interfaces for polymorphism. Prefer small, focused interfaces (`io.Reader`, `io.Writer`). Compose complex behavior by embedding multiple small types. This is idiomatic Go — avoid deep type hierarchies.
